# Local triage setup with GitHub Copilot

Use a dedicated local checkout and Copilot automation to produce read-only issue and PR triage digests. The checkout can live anywhere on your machine; no particular directory or Copilot project name is required.

## One-time setup

1. **Install and authenticate the tools.** Set up the GitHub Copilot app with access to local repository sessions and Automations, plus Git and the GitHub CLI (`gh`). Sign in to Copilot and authenticate `gh` with an account that can read `adobe/react-spectrum`. Verify access with `gh auth status` and `gh repo view adobe/react-spectrum`. Do not put credentials or tokens in prompts or repository files.
2. **Prepare a dedicated checkout.** Create a separate clone or worktree of `adobe/react-spectrum` for triage rather than using your active development checkout. Ensure `origin` points to the intended repository and that the checkout contains the approved `.github/triage/` rules. If those files are not on the default branch yet, use the maintainer-provided rules branch/ref. Set up the local `triage_support` branch before creating the automation; this is the branch convention used by the current rules and entry prompts, not a required filesystem path. Do not ask the running automation to create or switch branches.
3. **Add the checkout to Copilot.** Open or add that local repository in the Copilot app under a name of your choice. Select it as the repository for the automations. Use the existing-checkout/branch workspace option so runs use this dedicated checkout instead of silently creating another worktree. Record the expected absolute checkout root in the local automation configuration or prompt, not in this shared document.
4. **Configure separate issue and PR automations.** In Copilot's Automations view, choose the local execution environment and this repository. Use the corresponding entry prompt from [automation-prompts.md](automation-prompts.md), which loads [issues.md](issues.md) or [pull-requests.md](pull-requests.md). Add the expected checkout root to the local prompt for the verification step below. Choose schedules that suit your team, but keep the automations disabled until their prompts, permissions, and checkout have been reviewed.
5. **Review authorization explicitly.** The entry prompts record an existing automation-only authorization for Git synchronization and digest commits. Copying that text does not grant authorization for another person's setup. Approve those operations explicitly for your configured automation, or omit that authorization and keep digest commits disabled. These instructions never authorize interactive sessions to fetch, merge, stage, or commit. Never allow a digest run to commit rule or initiative changes.
6. **Verify a manual dry run before scheduling.** Run each configured automation manually after approving its read-only scope. Confirm that it uses the intended checkout and branch, skips verified team-authored analysis, writes only its digest, and makes no GitHub changes. Check the digest's proposed labels, evidence, and limitations before enabling recurring runs. A local automation requires its host machine to be available at run time.

The local configuration needs only the expected checkout root, the issue or PR entry prompt, the chosen schedule, and explicit Git-operation permissions. Keep credentials outside the repository and keep triage behavior in the shared rule files rather than maintaining divergent scheduler copies.

## Current rollout boundary

GitHub remains read-only while bot-token setup and explicit enablement are pending. Existing read credentials may be used for dry runs; token availability alone never enables writes. The intended first live phase is labels only, not comments. Do not enable, reschedule, or change the execution host of automations merely because these documents were edited.

Cloud execution and the label-driven lifecycle are tracked separately in [the label-driven triage initiative](initiatives/label-driven-triage.md); secure reproduction access is tracked in [the secure reproduction initiative](initiatives/secure-reproductions.md). Neither initiative grants runtime permissions. A local dry run must not retrieve or execute untrusted reproduction code.

## Per-run setup (run before triage)

Follow the selected entry prompt and its rule file. The only permitted Git mutations are explicitly authorized fetching, merging `origin/main`, and committing the generated digest to `triage_support`. Never push, create or switch branches, rewrite history (rebase, amend, reset, or force), or stage/commit files outside `.github/triage/tmp-digests/`. Do not modify another checkout.

1. **Verify the checkout and branch.** Compare `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` with the expected checkout root configured locally, and confirm `git branch --show-current` prints `triage_support`. Verify the repository identity with `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`. If the expected root is not configured, the repository is not `adobe/react-spectrum`, or the checkout/branch differs, stop and report the mismatch. Do not infer the expected root from wherever the process happens to start, or switch branches to recover.
2. **Fetch only when authorized.** Run `git fetch origin` only with the configured automation's explicit synchronization authorization. Otherwise skip synchronization and note the source revision and limitation in the digest. If fetching fails, report it and do not claim the source is current.
3. **Update against main only when safe and authorized.** After a successful authorized fetch, use `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` to check for any tracked changes, including changes under `.github/triage/`. If there are none and no merge/rebase is already in progress, run `git merge origin/main --no-edit`. Never overwrite untracked files that block the merge. If the merge conflicts, abort only the merge started by this run with `git merge --abort`, continue with the un-updated branch, and note the conflict at the top of the digest. If changes or an existing Git operation prevent synchronization, skip the merge and report why; do not stash, reset, or resolve someone else's work.
4. **Write the digest; commit only when authorized.** Write the issue or PR digest under `.github/triage/tmp-digests/` using the relevant rule file's Output section. If a file at the chosen path already exists, preserve it and stop for maintainer direction rather than overwrite an earlier run. Before staging, check `git diff --cached --name-only`; if anything is already staged, leave the index untouched and report that the digest was not committed. With explicit digest-commit authorization and an empty index, stage only the new digest and commit it on `triage_support` with `chore: add <PR|issue> triage digest YYYY-MM-DD` and the trailer `Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>`. Without authorization, leave the digest uncommitted and report that explicitly. Never push.
5. **Report the actual result.** Put the branch, source `origin/main` revision used (or the synchronization failure/skip reason), the digest's path in this checkout, and its commit hash at the top of the final message. If no commit was made, say so instead of inventing a hash. Finish with a short summary. Do not claim labels, comments, notifications, or other GitHub changes were made in a dry run.
